document_metadata.document_title: Maine Stormwater Management Design Manual, Volume III (capital MS4)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Treat the first 1 inch of runoff from impervious surfaces and 0.4 inch from landscaped areas.

evidence.excerpt: City of Augusta capital MS4 follows Maine Stormwater Design Manual Vol III
Treat the first 1 inch of runoff from impervious surfaces and 0.4 inch from landscaped areas
An underdrained soil filter must detain and filter a runoff volume equal to 1.0 inch times the subcatchment's impervious area plus 0.4 inch times the subcatchment's landscaped developed area.
A filter basin must drain dry in no less than 24 and no more than 48 hours.
The soil filter over the gravel underdrain pipe bedding must be at least 18 inches deep and must extend across the entire filter area.
The peak water quality storage depth should not exceed 6 inches over a bioretention basin filter.
Provide a long and narrow basin shape, with a minimum 2:1 length to width ratio (3:1 is best).
A minimum slope of 2% is considered normal for extensive and simple intensive greening.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Municipality coverage via Maine Stormwater Management Design Manual Volume III.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: WQv sizing is explicit as 1.0 inch on impervious plus 0.4 inch on landscaped developed area (Atlas and Ch. 7.1/7.2/7.4). SHWT separation is stated as 12 inches (1 foot) for detention basins, bioretention, and subsurface sand filters, and 18 inches for grassed underdrained soil filters—no single manual-wide minimum was applied. Gravel wetland target detention is a 24–48 hour range. Pervious surface text gives infiltration bounds (<2.41 in/hr, >0.04 in/hr) and 1 inch+ storage capacity, not a single storage section depth. Proprietary systems use Maine DEP approval letters (Appendix B), not TAPE/NJCAT by name.
